summary: USB-C dock NIC priority swap corrupts SCCM task sequence on Lenovo X1 after image
description:
Issue summary:
During post-image provisioning in the US-West imaging lab we observed intermittent SCCM Task Sequence failures on Lenovo X1 devices when a USB-C dock is attached. The failure correlates with dock-driven NIC priority/metric changes that occur mid-task-sequence, causing the machine to briefly lose access to the SCCM distribution point and fail Download Package steps.

Impact:
- Blocks automated provisioning for new Lenovo X1 devices in lab and blocks a small batch of new hires (10 devices).
- Manual re-run of Task Sequence sometimes succeeds if dock is removed.
- Affects throughput of imaging lab by ~30% when docked units are present.

Environment:
- Lab: Imaging Rack B (prod-us-west) using SCCM Current Branch 2211 task sequences.
- Boot method: WinPE -> SCCM OSD 1.3.5 task sequence -> Windows 11 22H2 corporate image.
- Dock model in repro: CalDigit TS4 and OEM Lenovo USB-C docks.
- Affected models: Lenovo X1 Carbon Gen 11, X1 Yoga Gen 7.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Boot device into WinPE and start SCCM Task Sequence from lab server (PXE/TS).
2) Attach USB-C dock either during PXE boot or immediately after OS payload apply.
3) Task Sequence begins Download Package step for the OOBE provisioning bundle.
4) At ~T+12m the machine flips network metric: onboard NIC drops to metric 50 and dock NIC inserted enumerates as interface with metric 10.
5) SCCM client loses connection to distribution point for ~20-40 seconds and Download Package fails with 0x80070002 / 0x87D00215.
6) Task Sequence either retries and eventually times out (fail) or succeeds if dock removed and task sequence restarted.

Recent logs / error traces:
- SCCM smsts.log snippet (hostname=IMAG-4102, 2026-03-10 14:12:23):
  DownloadPackage: PackageID=ABC00012, State=Failed, ErrorCode=0x87D00215
  Network status: Lost connectivity to DP (10.12.4.7) for 35s during transfer
- Windows event: 2026-03-10 14:12:12 System: NetworkAdapter EventID 27: "Network interface changed metric due to new adapter enumeration"
- WinPE: netsh interface show interface reports both NICs up with different metrics immediately prior to failure.

Initial hypothesis:
- USB-C dock exposes an additional Ethernet adapter which Windows assigns a lower route metric, causing transient route changes during driver initialization. SCCM OSD relies on steady DP connectivity; the metric flip causes the DP to be unreachable from current route until ARP/ND cache stabilizes.
- The task sequence does not wait or rebind the SCCM client to the new interface before starting large downloads.

Investigation performed so far:
- Reproduced locally in lab with two different dock vendors; failure rate ~40% when dock attached before or during payload apply.
- Captured packet traces on imaging switch; observed ARP refresh and short period of no response when dock NIC takes precedence.
- Tested toggling NIC metrics manually during OSD: forcing onboard NIC metric to be lower prevents failure; forcing dock NIC to lower metric reproduces failure deterministically.
- Cross-checked SCCM logs against INT-50321 (serial normalization issue) — likely unrelated but linked because affected batches overlapped.
- Filed a GH PR to add a short "network stabilization" wait step into OSD task sequence as a temporary mitigation (see related_github_prs).

Current status:
- Team has implemented a non-invasive workaround in a test Task Sequence: insert a 45s "Wait for network" step after network drivers initialize and before any large downloads. Test run shows failure rate dropped to ~5% in lab.
- Hardware team will test dock firmware update with CalDigit; Lenovo engineering asked for NIC driver logs.

Workaround (temporary):
- For immediate imaging needs, remove the USB-C dock during SCCM Task Sequence runs or apply the test Task Sequence with the network wait step.
- For bulk imaging, move Lenovo X1s to a dedicated rack where docks are not used during OSD.

Next steps / recommended fixes:
1) Short-term: Promote the network-stabilization step to the baseline Task Sequence across imaging racks and monitor failure rate for 48 hours. (Owner: IT-automation)
2) Mid-term: Add a small PowerShell check in WinPE that validates DP reachability (HTTP HEAD) before Download Package; retry with backoff if route changes detected. (Owner: SCCM team)
3) Long-term: Engage with dock vendors to see if NIC driver enumeration can be delayed until after SCCM client initialization or if a persistent metric can be configured via driver options. (Owner: Hardware)
4) Update imaging runbook on Confluence with dock guidance and include a checklist for lab technicians.

Business impact notes:
- Affected batch of 10 new hire machines are delayed; hiring manager notified and devices will be imaged using the workaround.
- No production customer impact; internal provisioning only.

investigation:
Technical detail: The Windows routing table flips because the dock Ethernet interface comes up after the onboard adapter and is assigned a lower metric (auto-metric behavior). In WinPE and early OSD, the SCCM client uses the OS route table to reach DPs; a mid-download metric change tears the TCP connection. Packet capture shows TCP retransmits and then a reset when the route becomes inconsistent. Verified that pinning metrics prevents the issue. Hypothesis: driver/firmware differences across dock vendors cause timing variance; Dell docks did not reproduce.
Proposed instrumentation: add an smsts preflight check that performs HTTP HEAD to DP URL and logs time-to-connect, interface used, and route table snapshot into smsts.log for future investigations.
workaround: Remove dock during imaging OR use the test Task Sequence containing a 45s network wait and DP HEAD-check. Communicated to lab technicians and hiring ops.
next_steps: 1) Promote wait step globally for 48-72h and monitor. 2) Implement DP HEAD-check PR from SCCM team. 3) Coordinate with CalDigit and Lenovo for driver/firmware mitigation. 4) Update Confluence runbook.
notes: This ticket should remain open until: baseline TS is updated, HEAD-check deployed, and vendor firmware follow-up completed. If failure rate remains >5% after fixes, escalate to infra leadership.
